text: Large language models, or LLMs, are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites, and articles. When you give an LLM a prompt, the quality of your instructions matters a lot. This is called prompt engineering. LLMs can write texts, answer questions, and translate languages. However, they also have limits. They sometimes make mistakes, give outdated information, or produce biased answers, so users should always check important facts themselves.
